standard.title: Manipulate complex sounds
standard.description: manipulate more complex sounds in spoken words and use knowledge of blending, segmenting, phoneme deletion and phoneme substitution to read and write words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students segment words into separate phonemes including consonant blends and clusters, and manipulate phonemes by addition, deletion and substitution to generate new words (AC9E1LY09/10). They have not yet applied these skills to more complex phoneme sequences including multi-phoneme blends and medial substitution.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can manipulate complex sounds in spoken words using blending, segmenting, deletion and substitution to read and write words.

nodes.label: Blending and segmenting complex patterns
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can blend and segment spoken words with more complex phoneme patterns — multi-consonant blends, digraphs within clusters — to support reading and writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Blend and segment a word with a consonant cluster or digraph (e.g. 'b-r-o-th-er', 'c-l-ou-d-y') correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Blend and segment a range of words with complex patterns — multi-consonant initial clusters, medial digraphs, final clusters — connecting spoken manipulation to written word recognition and production.
wider: Compare segmentation of words with similar-sounding clusters and discuss how spelling relates to the sounds (e.g. 'scratch' vs 'catch' — similar endings, different spellings)
Segment and blend words from different word families to identify common phoneme patterns

response_modes.reason: Blending and segmenting complex patterns requires accumulated practice — repeated application across many word examples builds the automatic phoneme-level processing needed for fluent reading and writing. Practice volume is more productive than widening pattern types before fluency is established.

nodes.hinge_reason: Fluent blending and segmenting of complex patterns is prerequisite for Node 2 deletion and substitution — students who cannot reliably segment complex words cannot accurately identify or manipulate the phoneme at a specified position.
success_criteria: Student correctly segments a word with a multi-phoneme cluster into its component sounds.
Student correctly blends a sequence of phonemes including a digraph or complex cluster into a recognisable word.

nodes.label: Deletion and substitution
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can delete or substitute phonemes in spoken words — at initial, medial and final positions — to form new words.
nodes.minimum_width: Delete or substitute a phoneme at a specified position in a spoken word to form a new word (e.g. delete 'scr' from 'scratch' to get 'atch'; substitute medial vowel in 'stack' to get 'stick').
nodes.typical_width: Apply deletion and substitution at initial, medial and final positions across a range of words, connecting spoken manipulation to reading and writing new words.
wider: Generate word families through systematic substitution at a single position and discuss what the pattern reveals about English sound-spelling relationships
Apply deletion and substitution to read new words encountered during reading rather than only in isolation
success_criteria: Student correctly deletes a phoneme at a specified position in a spoken word.
Student correctly substitutes a phoneme at a specified position to form a new word.
